entries.name: Date palm
entries.leaves: evergreen pinnate fronds to 5 m, spiny petiole
entries.flowers: small cream, on pendant spadices; dioecious, hand-pollinated in groves
entries.fruit: ovoid drupes, sugary, 4-7 cm, yellow to dark brown
entries.voxel_shape: tall smooth ringed trunk, 15-25 fronds exploding from the summit
entries.notes: The oasis tree: a date grove means the water table is within reach. Fruits feed whole regions of North Africa and Arabia.

entries.name: Saguaro
entries.leaves: none; spines only, succulent fluted stem
entries.flowers: large white, nocturnal, May-June, bats and bees
entries.voxel_shape: thick fluted column, 0-50 upward curving arms
entries.notes: The Sonoran icon. First arms appear at about 75 years; the oldest known specimens approach 300. Freeze-sensitive.

entries.name: Indian fig prickly pear
entries.leaves: flat fleshy pads (cladodes) with spines and glochids
entries.voxel_shape: stacked oval pads, spines as single-block bumps
entries.notes: The most widespread cactus on Earth; glochids are tiny barbed spines that detach at a touch.

entries.name: Creosote bush
entries.leaves: small waxy dark-green pairs, resinous, fragrant after rain
entries.voxel_shape: low rounded dome of slender green twigs, gaps in the centre on old plants
entries.notes: Individual shrubs live about a century, but the 11,700-year-old clonal ring 'King Clone' in the Mojave may be the oldest living organism on Earth.

entries.name: Honey mesquite
entries.leaves: bipinnate, fine leaflets
entries.voxel_shape: short trunk splitting low into thorny, drooping branches
entries.notes: Taproots to 30 m reach deep groundwater; pods fed whole regions of the American Southwest.

entries.name: Blue palo verde
entries.leaves: tiny bipinnate leaflets, dropped early; green bark photosynthesises
entries.voxel_shape: wispy green-barked trunk, sparse nearly leafless crown of yellow
entries.notes: Green branches do the photosynthesis. A key nurse tree: saguaros seedling under its shade.

entries.name: Ocotillo
entries.leaves: small oval leaves that appear within days of rain, dropped in drought
entries.voxel_shape: a dozen whip-thin whips rising from the base, bare or briefly leafed
entries.notes: Looks dead most of the year; leafs out within days of rain. Used as a living thorn fence across the Southwest.

entries.name: Joshua tree
entries.leaves: stiff blue-green daggers to 40 cm in terminal rosettes
entries.fruit: green dry berry; obligate pollination by yucca moths
entries.voxel_shape: single trunk, few thick forking limbs, each tipped with a spiky rosette
entries.notes: A monocot, not a true tree; named by Mormon settlers seeing raised arms like Joshua praying. Classically Mojave.

entries.name: Fishhook barrel cactus
entries.leaves: none; hooked radial spines, 20-27 ribs
entries.voxel_shape: ribbed barrel, slightly leaning south in old age
entries.notes: Old plants lean toward the equator, earning the name 'compass barrel'; spines form a hooked crown.

entries.name: Teddybear cholla
entries.leaves: none; dense pale microspines on every joint
entries.voxel_shape: fuzzy-looking shrub of silvery-spined joints; do not touch
entries.notes: The 'jumping cactus': joints detach to grip anything brushing past; spines are barbed and hard to remove.

entries.name: Organ pipe cactus
entries.leaves: none; many fluted stems from the base
entries.voxel_shape: clutch of upright fluted organ pipes from one base
entries.notes: A Sonoran speciality of the frost-free belt; named for its cluster of upright pipes like a church organ.

entries.name: Cardon
entries.leaves: none; 10-16 ribs per stem
entries.voxel_shape: massive multi-branched column, arms from the base like a saguaro writ large
entries.notes: The tallest cactus in the world (19.2 m recorded); 'elephant cactus' of the Baja cactus forests (cardonales).

entries.name: Ghaf tree
entries.leaves: bipinnate, drought-evergreen
entries.fruit: pods eaten green as sangri and dried
entries.voxel_shape: spreading crown on a short thorny trunk, nearly always green
entries.notes: National tree of the UAE and state tree of Rajasthan; taproot to ~30 m keeps it green through hyper-arid months.

entries.name: Camel thorn
entries.leaves: blue-green bipinnate, closes in heat
entries.voxel_shape: flat-topped spreading crown on a forked trunk, long white thorns
entries.notes: Roots reported to 60 m; a keystone of Kalahari sandveld, feeding giraffes, cattle, and people. Protected in South Africa.

entries.name: Desert ironwood
entries.leaves: pinnate, bluish-green, semi-evergreen
entries.voxel_shape: low thorny trunk with dense rounded canopy, often multi-trunked
entries.notes: Wood so dense it sinks and resists fire; the old-growth giant of Sonoran bajadas, sheltering young saguaros.

entries.name: Desert willow
entries.leaves: long narrow willow-like leaves on arching whips
entries.voxel_shape: fountain of drooping willow-like branches, few leaves, bell flowers
entries.notes: Not a willow at all (a catalpa relative); a washes specialist that blooms for weeks after summer storms.

entries.name: Doum palm
entries.leaves: fan-shaped costapalmate, in forked crowns
entries.voxel_shape: one of few palms that forks Y-like, up to 8 crowns on one trunk
entries.notes: A groundwater indicator along the Nile and wadis; cultivated in Egypt since the Pharaohs; 1 of ~11 branching palm species.

entries.name: Desert date
entries.leaves: two leaflets, semi-evergreen, thorny branchlets
entries.voxel_shape: leaning green-thorned shrub-tree, flat crown
entries.notes: The Sahel's survival tree: fruit, oil, fodder and soap from one drought-hardy plant; a Great Green Wall favourite.

entries.name: Fourwing saltbush
entries.leaves: silvery-grey narrow leaves, salt-excreting
entries.voxel_shape: low grey cushion shrub; the classic western rangeland browse
entries.notes: A saltbush: pumps salt out through leaves. Prized browse and a reclamation plant for disturbed rangeland.

entries.name: Brittlebush
entries.leaves: silvery-white in drought, green after rain
entries.voxel_shape: low mounded shrub, silvery between rains, yellow after them
entries.notes: Silver leaves reflect heat and fold flat in drought; blooms in waves after winter rain.

entries.name: Desert marigold
entries.leaves: silvery woolly, lobed
entries.flowers: bright yellow daisy discs, nearly year-round after rain
entries.voxel_shape: small woolly clump with round yellow suns on thin stalks
entries.notes: A staple of Sonoran and Mojave road verges; needs nothing but alkaline gravel and sun.

entries.name: Athel tamarisk
entries.leaves: scale-like, salt-excreting, cedar-like
entries.voxel_shape: soft feathery conical crown on a short trunk, deep-rooted
entries.notes: Drinks deep groundwater and sweats salt onto its leaves. Invasive in the American West, a classic shade tree of Arabia.

entries.name: Death Valley ephedra
entries.leaves: nearly none; jointed green stems do the work
entries.voxel_shape: wiry tangle of jointed pale stems, leafless
entries.notes: A gnetophyte, closer to conifers than to flowering plants; 'Mormon tea' relatives gave the world ephedrine.

entries.name: Desert agave
entries.leaves: rigid blue-grey swords with terminal spines
entries.flowers: tall spike of yellow blooms, then the plant dies
entries.voxel_shape: ball of rigid radiating leaves on rocky slopes
entries.notes: Monocarpic: one spectacular flower stalk, then death. CAM photosynthesis; grows where rain fails for years.

entries.name: Aloe vera
entries.leaves: fleshy spotted rosettes, serrated edges
entries.voxel_shape: spiky succulent rosette, spreading by offsets into clumps
entries.notes: Almost never sets seed; spreads by offsets. Probably native to Arabia, now naturalised everywhere warm and dry exists.

entries.name: Desert rose
entries.leaves: leathery obovate leaves, clustered at shoot tips
entries.flowers: salverform pink to crimson, year-round in warmth
entries.voxel_shape: bottle-shaped caudex with stubby leafless-to-leafy branches
entries.notes: Pachycaul caudex may exceed 1 m wide; milky latex is cardenolide-toxic; a Sahel and Arabian houseplant-on-steroids.

entries.name: Welwitschia
entries.leaves: two permanent strap leaves, never shed, torn to ribbons by wind
entries.flowers: cones; separate sexes; gnetophyte, not a flowering plant
entries.voxel_shape: low woody cone of two endless frayed leaves lying flat; unmistakable
entries.notes: Two leaves for its whole life, some specimens older than 1500 years; lives almost entirely on Namib fog; 'living fossil' unique to Namibia and southern Angola.

entries.name: Boojum tree
entries.leaves: tiny leaves after rare rains; mostly a wand of spines
entries.voxel_shape: upside-down carrot: fat tapering trunk with short horizontal spikes
entries.notes: Baja endemic relative of the ocotillo, named via Carroll's Snark; the tallest known was 26 m. Protected; slower than the cardon.

entries.name: Quiver tree
entries.leaves: grey-green succulent leaves in terminal rosettes
entries.voxel_shape: smooth pale forking trunk, symmetric umbrella of rosettes
entries.notes: San hunters hollowed branches for quivers; a succulent tree listed Vulnerable, sliding as the Kalahari warms.

entries.name: Hoodia
entries.leaves: none; finger-like spiny succulent stems
entries.voxel_shape: cluster of upright spiny fingers from one base
entries.notes: San hunters chewed stems to dull hunger on long marches; now a regulated appetite-suppressant trade with San benefit-sharing.

entries.name: Frankincense tree
entries.leaves: pinnate, deciduous, clustered at branch tips
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled multi-stemmed tree on limestone ledges, papery peeling bark
entries.notes: Incisions bleed a milky sap that hardens to olibanum, traded since 1500 BC; Dhofar and Somalia supply most of the world's incense.

entries.name: Myrrh tree
entries.leaves: trifoliate, shed to bare twigs in drought
entries.voxel_shape: small thorny tree with straggling branches, often leafless
entries.notes: One of the three gifts of the Magi; gum-bearing (Commiphora); tapped like frankincense for 'bitter tears' of resin.

entries.name: Socotra dragon blood tree
entries.leaves: stiff dark-green straps in dense terminal tufts, shed every 3-4 years
entries.voxel_shape: giant green umbrella: mushroom crown on a bare grey trunk
entries.notes: Socotra endemic; the resin bled red like blood and was medieval Europe's universal varnish and medicine. Vulnerable, failing to regenerate under goat grazing.

entries.name: Camel grass
entries.leaves: long aromatic blades, citrus-scented
entries.voxel_shape: tussock of tall arching aromatic blades
entries.notes: The 'camel grass' of Arabian wadis; citronella-like oil used in teas and folk medicine; marks deeper sands.

entries.name: Hard spinifex
entries.leaves: needle-sharp in-rolled leaves, resinous domes up to 2 m wide
entries.voxel_shape: spiky yellow-green hummock, hollow dead centre in old rings
entries.notes: Covers a quarter of Australia; old hummocks become rings 40-50 years old; one of the most flammable landscapes on Earth, key for Aboriginal fire-stick farming.

entries.name: Bitter apple
entries.leaves: lobed grey-green, sand-camouflaged
entries.fruit: smooth mottled sphere, small watermelon-like, intensely bitter
entries.voxel_shape: straggling sand-hugging vine; round fruits half-buried in dust
entries.notes: The 'apple of Sodom': looks like a tiny melon, empties the bowel with terrible force; biblical purgative never to be eaten casually.

entries.name: Rose of Jericho
entries.leaves: small grey hairy leaves, dry into a ball
entries.voxel_shape: a tumbleweed ball; 'resurrects' and unfurls when wetted
entries.notes: Not a rose: a mustard relative. Dies, curls into a ball, rolls with the wind; the 'resurrection plant' of folk magic and scripture.

entries.name: Desert truffle
entries.fruit: hypogeous ascoma, walnut-to-fist sized, near Helianthemum roots
entries.voxel_shape: underground knobs; nothing above ground until hunted
entries.notes: Mycorrhizal with rockroses (Helianthemum); erupts after autumn-winter rains in Arabian and Saharan depressions; a candidate for the biblical manna.

entries.name: Nara melon
entries.leaves: none; green spines photosynthesise
entries.fruit: spiny green melon to 15 cm, edible; seedy 'butterpips'
entries.voxel_shape: leafless thorny melon-bush trapping sand into hummocks to 1,500 m2
entries.notes: A leafless cucurbit 40 million years old; its sand hummocks trap dunes in place; the Topnaar people of the Kuiseb have eaten it for millennia.

entries.name: Mulga
entries.leaves: silver-grey phyllodes channelling rain to the taproot
entries.voxel_shape: dense silver-grey wattle shrub to small tree, evenly spaced
entries.notes: 'Mulga country' is a quarter of Australia; honey ants nest beneath the roots; one of the longest-lived acacias, to 300-400 years.
